Culīna et potūs · Kitchen, meals & drinks

saucepan in Latin

saucepan

ōlla ānsāta

Neo-LatinDraft
  • ōlla ānsāta — saucepan, a pot with a handle modern (M-O s.v. pan: saucepan)12

See also: cooking pot.

  1. ōlla has a long o: it is the later form of aula. Ruling: ōlla with a long o
  2. The vowel before ns is long, so ānsāta, from ānsa, a handle.
Sources & evidence

Lewis & Short: olla · Lewis & Short: ansatus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. pan: saucepan, pan: pot, cutlery: spoon: slotted spoon, sieve, sieve: colander, grater: cheese-grater, wire whisk, press: garlic press.

Draft of 8 November 2026, not yet reviewed.
